body:
Lean accepts complete original Python function bodies inside `triton { ... }`. Caller types, values, constexpr settings and compilation configuration stay outside the quotation. Casts, branches, masks, helpers and operation order remain visible; actual execution connects to independent mathematics and complete IO judgments.

Coverage: **117 / 183 selected tasks; 19 / 19 examples; 413 checked raw-body mappings. 66 tasks remain.** Examples without historical Python document authored or independently specification-derived Python sources.

Keep this PR **draft**. **Do not merge before the user's review.** The migration is ongoing.

### Latest completed checkpoint: persistent matrix multiplication

The complete original and existing row-product-commuted Python bodies have four exact FP16/E4M3 body/ABI mappings. All 16 top-level statements remain: int64 casts, simultaneous metadata assignments, Boolean ceiling arithmetic, persistent tile and K loops, clamped pointers, live FP32 dot and output-dtype branches. Full Python module AST restoration permits exactly the row-index product operand commutation. Original Python, public Real/FP readers and contracts remain unchanged.

Exact signed prefix arithmetic derives the source counts and register invariants. Complete grid execution, trace safety, outputs and exterior frames reconnect to the independent full-K formula and actual FP source pair. The raw body is re-proved directly; no equality to the historical rewritten AST is assumed. The public FP comparison prints no numerical assumptions. Zero axes, tails, strides, aliasing and the existing input-word domain remain. Optional native/Tensor results retain their explicit instruction and physical-model boundaries.

The frontend now widens Boolean operands to signed zero or one in integer arithmetic. A symbolic regression covers both operand orders, subtraction, multiplication and inline predicates. No `sorry`, new axiom, whole-kernel premise, arbitrary FP cast identity or public-domain restriction is introduced.

### Verification for source `3ac09beb9da8fe5ceab10a2c855c683a67e45afd`

- **48 focused roots plus joint import pass**, with 716 theorem footprints checked during development. Failed intermediate diagnostics are retained.
- **5572 cumulative modules plus joint import pass**, warm and independently from an empty project build directory. Only pinned external packages are reused; no other project objects or `.veritile-cache` are imported.
- **7026 local Lean source files** in the complete import closure match Git byte for byte.
- **37290 theorems across 1855 defining modules**, including private helpers, pass the standard-base axiom audit.
- **347 targeted Python tests pass.** The full **592-test** run retains one known pre-existing import error: an old numerical receipt no longer matches unchanged `Structural.lean`. The affected numerical-binding test module cannot load; its hash was not falsely repinned.
- **50 actual official comparator attempts are UNAVAILABLE** because the host provides Landlock ABI v4 instead of required v5 and lacks systemd user isolation. No bypass. Torch/Triton are absent. These unavailable checks do not count as passing; no GPU or new numerical experiment was run.
- Formula, IO/reader organization, progress and body-correspondence guards pass on the exact receipt.

Ongoing follow-up: ordinary integer-literal assignments need tensor creation and conversion semantics distinct from inline weak scalars. The fix is under development, and five previously mapped task families are being rechecked. `add_value` has passed its targeted execution/FP reproof with an explicit strict integer-literal certificate. LoRA now passes the targeted complete execution, safety and public IO/Real/FP reproof; Fast RoPE passes its actual signed-loop execution, safety and source-pair proofs. The full affected-family regression remains in progress. Separately, two-pass LayerNorm has passed its focused proof checks and warm cumulative build; the independent empty-project-cache replay is still running. These development changes are not in the published checkpoint above. Coverage counts describe registered body mappings; complete semantic migration and generic frontend support are not yet claimed.

Evidence: [`native-persistent-matmul-function-bodies`](https://github.com/VeriInfra-Lab/VeriTile/tree/efab0901780251409b7b6a9759fa7c1d5f23cebb/bench/review-checkpoints/2026-10-29/native-persistent-matmul-function-bodies). Previous checkpoints retain their original validation scopes and limitations, including matrix multiplication, BGMV shrink and multinomial sampling. These are proofs in the stated project models, not a blanket hardware-conformance claim.
